svg.aria-label: Four ways an AI exam score is wired into a screening programme, with the evidence for each. One: triage, as in the Swedish MASAI randomised trial: low-score exams get one reader, high-score exams get two readers with AI marks; sensitivity rose from 73.8 to 80.5 percent, specificity stayed 98.5 percent, interval cancers 1.55 versus 1.76 per 1,000. Two: safety net and normal triaging, as in the German PRAIM real-world study of 463,094 women: detection rose from 5.7 to 6.7 per 1,000 with recall 37.4 versus 38.3 per 1,000. Three: partially autonomous, as in the Spanish paired trial of 31,301 women: AI low-risk exams are reported normal without a reader; workload fell 63.6 percent and detection rose 15.2 percent, but recall rose 14.8 percent and a few cancers were in the low-risk group. Four: certified dismissal, as in the TRUST paper: the dismissal threshold is set so a one-sided 99 percent upper bound on cancer prevalence among dismissed exams holds; it dismissed about 20 percent of cases on NLBS at 95 to 98 percent recall targets.
svg.title: Four ways to wire an AI exam score into screening
svg.text: Same score, four workflows: where the threshold sits decides what the AI is
Per-exam malignancy score from one detector/classifier → routing rule. Numbers are as reported in each study; settings differ and are not directly comparable.

g.text: ① Triage — MASAI RCT (Sweden, ~105K women; Lancet 2026)
low score → single reader · high score → double reader with AI marks
sensitivity 73.8% → 80.5% · specificity 98.5% both arms · interval cancers 1.76 → 1.55 / 1,000 (non-inferior)
fewer invasive, T2+ and non-luminal-A interval cancers
② Normal-triage + safety net — PRAIM (Germany, 463,094 women; Nat Med 2025)
double reading stays; AI tags confident normals and alerts on missed suspicious exams
observational, radiologists chose whether to use the AI-supported viewer
③ Partially autonomous — paired trial (Spain, 31,301 women, DM + DBT; Nat Med 2026)
AI low-risk → reported normal with no reader · rest → double reading with AI support
a small number of cancers fell in the AI low-risk group
④ Certified dismissal — TRUST (research, arXiv 2609.00300, Sep 2026)
threshold chosen so a one-sided 99% Clopper–Pearson bound on cancer rate among dismissed exams holds;
threshold is recomputed during training and positives near it are penalised
NLBS: 19.74% / 21.70% of cases dismissed at 98% / 95% recall · RSNA: 7.04 → 14.31% and 13.49 → 19.69%
